source.section: Military Retirement Income Exemption Worksheet questions 1-3 and Lines 4-10 (booklet PDF p.17; IN-112 Instructions PDF pp.3-4 Line 13); Schedule IN-112 Part I Line 13 (booklet PDF p.23); Line 13 'may claim one additional exclusion' (booklet PDF p.33; IN-112 Instructions PDF p.4); Retirement Income Exemption Worksheet, Sections I and II (booklet PDF p.16; IN-112 Instructions PDF p.2); Schedule IN-112 Part I Line 12 (booklet PDF p.23); Form IN-111 Lines 1-8 and 14 (booklet PDF pp.10-11), standard deduction chart and Lines 4-5e (PDF p.11), rate schedules (PDF p.46)

worked: Federal taxable Social Security: provisional income = other income 58,170.00 + half of benefits 6,000.00 = 64,170.00; 85% x (64,170.00 - 44,000.00) + 6,000.00 = 23,144.50, limited to 85% x 12,000.00 = 10,200.00; taxable 10,200.00. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 1) 38,170.00 + military retirement pay (DFAS 1099-R) (person 0) 20,000.00 + taxable Social Security 10,200.00 = 68,370.00. Federal taxable income = 68,370.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 35,270.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form IN-111, Married Filing Jointly: Line 1 federal AGI 68,370.00. Schedule IN-112 Part I: Line 1 all state and local obligation interest 0.00; Line 2 Vermont obligations 0.00; Line 3 = 0.00; Line 4 0.00; Line 6 total additions 0.00. Retirement Income Exemption Worksheet (Social Security elected): question 2, AGI 68,370.00 is less than 80,000.00; question 3, less than 70,000.00: full exemption, Form 1040 Line 6b 10,200.00. Line 12 10,200.00. Military Retirement Income Exemption Worksheet: question 2, AGI 68,370.00 is less than 175,000.00; question 3, not over 125,000.00: full exemption of the military retirement pay 20,000.00. Line 13 20,000.00. Subtractions: Line 12 retirement benefits (Social Security) 10,200.00; Line 13 military retirement 20,000.00; Line 18 total subtractions 30,200.00. Line 19 net modifications = 0.00 - 30,200.00 = -30,200.00. Form IN-111 Line 2 -30,200.00; Line 3 = 68,370.00 + (-30,200.00) = 38,170.00. Line 4 standard deduction 15,300.00 + 1 x 1,250.00 age box(es) = 16,550.00 [person 0 born 1958-04-04 (65 or older: box checked), person 1 born 1967-06-06 (not born before Jan. 2, 1961: no box)]. Line 5a-5d personal exemptions 2; Line 5e 2 x 5,300.00 = 10,600.00. Line 6 = 16,550.00 + 10,600.00 = 27,150.00. Line 7 Vermont taxable income = 38,170.00 - 27,150.00 = 11,020.00. Line 8: schedule tax on 11,020.00 (Schedule Y-1, booklet p.46, merged continuous schedule): 3.35% x (11,020.00 - 0.00) = 369.17; the tax table (pp.47-51) gives 370. Federal AGI 68,370.00 is not greater than 150,000.00, so no minimum tax: Line 8 369.17. Line 9 0.00 (no Schedule IN-119 items; Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled not modelled); Line 10 369.17; Lines 11-13 0.00; Line 14 Vermont income tax 369.17.
accepted_approximations: The rate schedule is one continuous schedule: the printed rows that restart at 75,000 are merged and printed base taxes, rounded to the dollar, are not used. Below 75,000 the booklet uses tax tables in 100 dollar rows.
